title: UFH source-to-scored-question author audit
status: Manual source-fact mapping completed for this medicine; not independently clinically certified; selected questions await regenerated-runtime inspection
method: Manually separate important claims in the latest teaching fields, including the explicitly taught no-IM route fact missed by mechanical source-statement splitting. Count coverage only when knowing the source fact is necessary to get the scored answer; a fact printed in a stem or in a distractor gets no coverage credit.
notes: This targeted audit does not change overall 82-medication certification counts.
Previously repeated concentration-doubling MCQ is replaced by a medication-specific numeric pump-rate calculation; not a recommended clinical dosing regimen.
The previous generic bleeding-recognition MCQ remains a question-quality gap and is NOT credited here.
Actual local UFH protocol, bag concentrations, lab monitoring method and authorizations must be checked with the facility before clinical use.
Independent clinician review of all keys, choices and clinical applicability remains required.

facts.rationale: The medicine label already discloses 'UFH'; a rote class item would be answer-cued. The anticoagulant role and mechanism are tested separately.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Binds antithrombin and accelerates inhibition of thrombin and factor Xa.
facts.rationale: The principal-action question requires the antithrombin/thrombin/Xa mechanism.
The treatment-role question asks about prevention of thrombus propagation.
A new prophylaxis-specific SC UFH question requires identification of VTE prevention.
SC is stated in a prophylaxis question stem, not required to select its correct answer; do not credit that wording as testing route selection.

facts.sourceExcerpt: or IV depending on the order
facts.rationale: The bag/pump scenario involves IV UFH but does not directly ask the route distinction.
The heparin-route short-answer question requires recall of IM avoidance.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Therapeutic IV infusion requires a controlled pump
facts.rationale: The infusion question requires pump-rate calculation but the need for a controlled pump is supplied in the stem.

facts.fact: Verify strength and distinguish treatment from catheter-flush heparin
facts.sourceExcerpt: do not confuse a treatment vial with a catheter-flush product
facts.rationale: The heparin-infusion MCQ explicitly tests treatment vs flush strength.
The existing melena/pallor/hypotension item only asks to identify generic blood loss; the answer is inferable without knowing heparin. A targeted UFH nursing-response rewrite is pending.

facts.sourceExcerpt: aPTT or UFH-calibrated anti-Xa, as specified by local protocol
facts.rationale: The revised UFH coagulation question directly asks which response test guides authorized titration.

facts.sourceExcerpt: platelet counts and other safety labs
facts.rationale: HIT recognition is tested after a platelet fall, but the separate practice of scheduled platelet surveillance is not directly tested.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Do not independently change an infusion rate unless an authorized nurse-driven protocol applies
facts.rationale: The question requires escalation rather than an unsanctioned rate change.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Suspect HIT with a substantial unexpected platelet fall
facts.rationale: The existing HIT question requires connecting UFH exposure and platelet decline to HIT.

facts.fact: First action when HIT strongly suspected
facts.sourceExcerpt: promptly stop heparin and escalate for urgent assessment
facts.rationale: A new HIT-action question asks for immediate response to a marked platelet decline with new thrombosis.

facts.fact: Variability of UFH effect requires laboratory follow-up
facts.sourceExcerpt: UFH has a variable anticoagulant effect
facts.rationale: The revised monitoring question tests response measurements, but not a separate explanation of variability.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Therapeutic IV infusion requires a controlled pump after dilution
facts.rationale: An updated numeric-entry question requires calculating mL/hour from a hypothetical units/hour order and verified bag strength.
